There is some new metaprogramming that can help here: the `to_fun` attribute.
To get access, you need to add `import Mathlib.Tactic.ToFun` to the imports (doesn't need `public`).

```suggestion
@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma neg (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (-f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).neg

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma add (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (f + g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).add (hg x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
theorem sum (h : ∀ σ, Meromorphic (G σ)) :
    Meromorphic (∑ n ∈ s, G n) := fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.sum (h · x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma sub (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (f - g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).sub (hg x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma mul {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (f * g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).mul (hg x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
theorem prod (h : ∀ σ, Meromorphic (F σ)) :
    Meromorphic (∏ n ∈ s, F n) := fun x ↦ MeromorphicAt.prod (h · x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma div {f g : 𝕜 → 𝕜} (hf : Meromorphic f) (hg : Meromorphic g) :
    Meromorphic (f / g) := fun x ↦ (hf x).div (hg x)

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma pow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {n : ℕ} (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ (hf x).pow n

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma zpow {f : 𝕜 → 𝕜} {n : ℤ} (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (f ^ n) := fun x ↦ (hf x).zpow n

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]
lemma deriv [CompleteSpace E] (hf : Meromorphic f) : Meromorphic (deriv f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).deriv

@[to_fun (attr := fun_prop)]

    Meromorphic (_root_.deriv^[n] f) := fun x ↦ (hf x).iterated_deriv
```

(If so, which parts: all of it? what did you prompt it with? do you know the mathematics behind it? etc.) Please make this abundantly clear in the PR description, so we can review it properly.

As such, I don't think keeping this PR open is useful. If you have addressed all the above comments, feel free to re-open this PR.

Dear Jeff,

I'm happy to hear if my initial impression is wrong. (We are receiving a fair number of posts that are AI-generated with very little effort or understanding on the commenter's part, which is why I have a strong initial reaction about them. If yours is different, that is nice to hear; we definitely welcome high-quality contributions.)

To make this PR closer to mathlib standards, you should
- avoid any axioms: either fill them in (if they define data), deduce them from existing mathlib facts or state them as `sorry`. (This PR cannot be merged while it contains `sorry`'s, but this could indicate any missing gaps. I'm working towards the Sobolev embedding theorem, for example.)
- some definitions are simply shorter names for mathlib definitions (e.g. `fourier1D` or `smoothInTime`). In general, I would just inline those. (If you believe this is absolutely essential for readability, you can introduce an `abbrev`. This should be used sparingly.)
- note that the definitions of `fourierDecay` and `spectralNSResidual` (thus, by extension, `SolvesNavierStokes`), are vacuously true --- thus, very likely not what you intend. I haven't checked every definition in your PR; please do so carefully before submitting! The fact that this happened this should be a major red flag. In general, [this page](https://leanprover-community.github.io/did_you_prove_it.html) documents some common pitfalls with AI-generated proofs. source_comment_bodies:
I feel like this proof is too specialized for the homotopy category. Mathlib arleady knows that quotient categories of categories with unique objects and subsingleton homs have subsingleton homs, and that free categories on quivers with unique objects and unique homs have unique homs, 
so by adding
```lean
instance (V : Type*) [ReflQuiver V] [Unique V]
    [∀ (x y : V), Subsingleton (x ⟶ y)] (x y : FreeRefl V) :
    Subsingleton (x ⟶ y) :=
  letI (x y : V) : Unique (x ⟶ y) := by
    obtain rfl : x = y := by subsingleton
    exact (unique_iff_subsingleton_and_nonempty _ |>.mpr ⟨inferInstance, ⟨𝟙rq _⟩⟩).some
  inferInstance
```
around line 312 in `CategoryTheory/Category/ReflQuiv.lean`, and
```lean
instance [Subsingleton (X _⦋1⦌₂)] {x y : X _⦋0⦌₂} : Subsingleton (X.Edge x y) where
  allEq f g := by
    ext
    subsingleton
```

somewhere in `AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/CompStructTruncated.lean`, 

this becomes
```lean
instance subsingleton_hom (X : Truncated.{u} 2) [Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂)] [Subsingleton (X _⦋1⦌₂)]
    (x y : X.HomotopyCategory) :
    Subsingleton (x ⟶ y) :=
  letI : Unique (OneTruncation₂ X) := inferInstanceAs (Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂))
  letI (x y : (OneTruncation₂ X)) : Subsingleton (x ⟶ y) :=
    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton <| X.Edge _ _)
  CategoryTheory.Quotient.instSubsingletonHom _ _ _
```
which is IMO the "morally correct" proof (arguably, we could even consider registering the instances for OneTruncation on their own, but I’m not sure that would be very useful).

Same here: we already have `Cat.isTerminalOfUniqueOfIsDiscrete`:
```suggestion
instance (X : Truncated.{u} 2) [Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂)] : Unique X.HomotopyCategory := 
  letI : Unique (OneTruncation₂ X) := inferInstanceAs (Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂))
  CategoryTheory.Quotient.instUnique _

/-- If `X : Truncated 2` has a unique `0`-simplex and (at most) one `1`-simplex,
then `X.HomotopyCategory` is a terminal object in `Cat`. -/
def isTerminal (X : Truncated.{u} 2) [Unique (X _⦋0⦌₂)] [Subsingleton (X _⦋1⦌₂)] :
    IsTerminal (Cat.of X.HomotopyCategory) :=
  letI : IsDiscrete (X.HomotopyCategory) := { eq_of_hom := by subsingleton }
  Cat.isTerminalOfUniqueOfIsDiscrete
```
